verdicts.title: mpo_combine changed its documented exception type from KeyError to ConfigurationError (a ValueError) in a non-breaking commit
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual link verified. packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_mpo.py:56-63 and :70 now raise ConfigurationError; git show 7b26f655 -- .../_mpo.py shows both sites were `raise KeyError(...)` before and that the docstring 'Raises: KeyError' was rewritten to 'Raises: ConfigurationError' in the same hunk. packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27 defines `class ConfigurationError(OpaqueError, ValueError)` -- no LookupError/KeyError in the MRO, so `except KeyError:` no longer catches. mpo_combine is a genuine public export (packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/alignment/dpo/loss/__init__.py:41,78). The commit subject is `feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)` with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer, and `git tag --contains 7b26f655` shows it shipped in v0.15.4, v0.15.5 and v0.15.6.rc1. Two corrections to the finding's framing, neither of which defeats it: (a) the taxonomy docstring (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/exceptions/__init__.py:4-6) claims only that 'configuration, calibration, and privacy-budget errors are ValueError subclasses, while checkpoint failures are RuntimeError subclasses' -- it never markets KeyError preservation, and docs/reference/exceptions.md lists no KeyError family, so this is not an internal inconsistency the taxonomy promised to avoid; (b) _mpo.py was not singled out -- the same commit converted all five KeyError raises in the repo (2 in _mpo.py, 2 in _dp_trainer.py, 1 in _sft_trainer.py), so it is a uniform intentional policy, not an oversight in one file. What remains real is narrow and process-level: a released public function's documented exception type moved out of the LookupError hierarchy without the `!` / BREAKING CHANGE marker AGENTS.md requires, so it is not categorized as breaking in the changelog for v0.15.4. No privacy or numerical impact; the failure is loud either way (an uncaught ConfigurationError, not a wrong result).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Application code that calls the public `opaque.alignment.dpo.loss.mpo_combine` and guards the weights/losses key-mismatch with `except KeyError:` -- the contract the pre-7b26f655 docstring promised -- stops catching as of v0.15.4: the call now raises `opaque.exceptions.ConfigurationError`, which subclasses OpaqueError and ValueError but not LookupError/KeyError. The same swap was applied to two KeyError sites in _dp_trainer.py and one in _sft_trainer.py, so the exposure is three public-facing files, not one. The docstring, the docs table and the package's own test (tests/dpo/loss/test_mpo.py:59-63) were all updated in the same commit, so the change is documented and intentional; the only defect is that it shipped under a `feat` title with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer, so git-cliff does not list it as a breaking change for the v0.15.4 release line. No silent wrong results, no epsilon impact.

verdicts.title: torch_compile=True aborts on the first training step for every Hugging Face model: the fullgraph fallback was deleted, not narrowed
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end in this tree with the repo venv (torch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.15.1). packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:209-219 is a bare `torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` with no try/except; _grad_compiler at :4337-4369 wraps it in a lambda and threads it into every clipping factory as `_chunk_compiler` (:4412, :4425, :4437). packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:588-602 confirms the compiled `_chunk_kernel` body is `vmapped = _vmap(_per_example_fn, ...); outputs = vmapped(kernel_clipping_norm, *chunk_args)`, so the user's whole model forward sits inside the fullgraph region. `git show fae93a55` confirms it deleted `_compile_with_fullgraph_fallback` (the `except torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException` -> recompile with fullgraph=False wrapper) and replaced it with the strict version. My repro: LlamaForCausalLM(2 layers, hidden 32, vocab 32) + apply_runtime_patches + apply_model_patches, DPTrainer(torch_compile=True, torch_compile_backend='aot_eager', privacy_noise_multiplier=1.0) -> step 0 raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases` (hint text names `logger.warning_once`). Monkeypatching only `_compile_strict_chunk` to fullgraph=False on the identical run completes: train_loss 2.3148, 3 steps, eps 0.2308. Searched for an escape hatch and found none: docs/reference/transformers.md:218 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216 document the flag as 'compile ... with fullgraph=True' with no warning that HF models abort, there is no ignore_logging_functions registration anywhere in the tree, and the only end-to-end compile test (test_compile_and_kernel_args.py:112-140) uses a synthetic 2-layer nn.Module that emits no warning_once, so CI stays green. Severity held at medium rather than higher: torch_compile defaults to False, and the failure is a loud exception on step 1 -- no silent wrong results and no epsilon impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With `torch_compile=True` (non-default) on any real Hugging Face causal-LM under transformers 5.15.1, DPTrainer.train() raises on the first optimizer step with `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases`, because HF's forward calls `logger.warning_once` (use_return_dict deprecation / loss_type=None) inside the region compiled with fullgraph=True at _dp_trainer.py:209-219. Verified on LlamaForCausalLM(2 layers) with backend aot_eager and clipping_mode='fixed'; the identical run succeeds (3 steps, train_loss 2.3148) when _compile_strict_chunk is patched to fullgraph=False, which is exactly the fallback fae93a55 (#979) deleted. Fails loudly at step 1, so no wrong results are produced and no privacy claim is affected -- the documented flag is simply unusable on the model family opaque-transformers exists to serve, and the only end-to-end compile test uses a synthetic nn.Module that never triggers the warning.

verdicts.title: dynamic=True from the Poisson graph-reuse change makes clipping_mode="auto" + torch_compile crash even with no graph break
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently, and on an even simpler model than the finding used. `git show afa0247f` ('perf(transformers): reuse compiled graphs across Poisson batch shapes (#989)') confirms its only source change is adding `dynamic=True` to _compile_strict_chunk (_dp_trainer.py:209-219). My repro used a plain 2-layer nn.Module TinyLM (embedding + linear, no HF logging, so finding 33 cannot mask it) under DPTrainer(torch_compile=True, backend='aot_eager', per_device_train_batch_size=6, max_steps=3, privacy_noise_multiplier=1.0): clipping_mode='fixed' -> OK (loss 2.92617), 'adaptive' -> OK (loss 2.92621), 'auto' with clipping_kwargs={'gamma':0.01} -> `torch._dynamo.exc.SpeculationLogDivergence: SpeculationLog diverged at index 622 ... Expected: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/reparametrize_recompute.py:37 (STORE_ATTR) / Actual: :66 (CALL)`, i.e. the thread-local stack mutation in the _reparametrize_module patch. Flag sweep on the identical run isolates the cause to `dynamic=True` alone: fullgraph=True+dynamic=True FAIL; fullgraph=True+dynamic=False OK (loss 2.92617, bit-identical to the fixed-mode eager number); fullgraph=True+dynamic unset OK (identical). I additionally checked the combination the finding did not need but the fix for #33 would produce: fullgraph=False+dynamic=True on 'auto' also FAILS with the same divergence at index 622 -- so this is genuinely independent of finding 33 and would survive restoring the fullgraph fallback. Severity medium, not higher: two non-default options are required (torch_compile=True plus clipping_mode='auto') and the failure is a loud exception, not a silent numeric change; no epsilon impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: `TrainingArguments(clipping_mode='auto', clipping_kwargs={'gamma':0.01}, torch_compile=True)` makes DPTrainer.train() abort on the first compiled chunk with `torch._dynamo.exc.SpeculationLogDivergence` (diverging at the thread-local push in packages/opaque-patches/.../reparametrize_recompute.py:37 vs :66), while clipping_mode 'fixed' and 'adaptive' compile and run on the identical model, data and seed. Reproduced on a plain 2-layer nn.Module (no HF logging involved, so it is not the same defect as the fullgraph/warning_once failure) with backend aot_eager at batch size 6. The trigger is the explicit `dynamic=True` added by afa0247f (#989) at _dp_trainer.py:218: with dynamic=False or dynamic unset the same AUTO-S run completes with loss 2.92617, and the failure also reproduces with fullgraph=False, so it is independent of and would outlive a fix to the fullgraph fallback. Loud crash only -- no silent wrong gradients and no privacy impact. No engine-level test covers it: packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping/test_compile_chunks.py and packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/clipping/test_compile.py use pure tensor losses without the trainer's functional_call + reparametrize patch stack.

verdicts.title: compute_loss_func is now invoked at two different tensor ranks; a per-example loss silently reports a different eval objective
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced numerically. The two call sites are as claimed: _dp_trainer.py:2719-2726 calls `self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` on the BATCHED forward output in the default eval branch, while _dp_trainer.py:2452-2456 (compute_per_example_loss) calls the same callable under vmap with the leading batch dim stripped -- its own docstring at :2409-2412 says 'One example's input dict (under vmap; the caller stripped the leading batch dim)'. `git show 25bb4ed7` ('fix(transformers): honor custom loss during evaluation (#1028)') confirms the batched branch previously read `output.get('loss')` and carried a comment telling users to set include_for_metrics=['loss'] to get compute_loss_func honoured at eval; that comment and the guard were removed. Nothing validates the rank of the callable's inputs or of its return. My repro (T=V=4, plain dict-returning nn.Module, compute_loss_func = lambda out, labels: F.cross_entropy(out['logits'][:-1], labels[1:]), the documented per-example causal-LM shift): default evaluate() -> eval_loss 1.34594; include_for_metrics=['loss'] evaluate() -> 1.70644; hand-computed mean of per-example shifted CE over the same eval set -> 1.70644. So the default path is off by 0.36 nats with no exception, because the callable shifted along the batch axis and cross_entropy read the sequence axis as the class axis. Changing only V to 5 (T!=V) turns the same default eval into `RuntimeError: Expected target size [3, 5], got [3, 4]`, confirming the second half of the claim. The doc drift is real: docs/alignment/trainers.md:112-114 still says the SFT custom loss 'runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op', and packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:646-656 delegates every non-DFT loss_type to `super().prediction_step`, landing on the batched call. The tests added by 25bb4ed7 use only rank-agnostic losses (`cross_entropy(output['logits'], labels)` on 2-D logits), so none of them catch it. One correction: the token-weighted aggregation at :2946-2966 is now additionally gated on `self._is_causal_lm` (added by the same commit), so the compounding the finding describes applies to real HF causal LMs but not to the plain module I used -- I verified the gate exists but did not separately measure the token-weighting amplification. Severity medium: it requires a user-supplied compute_loss_func that is sensitive to the leading axis, affects only reported eval metrics (and through them best-model selection / early stopping), and has no effect on the training objective, gradients, noise or epsilon.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user passes `compute_loss_func=lambda out, labels: F.cross_entropy(out['logits'][:-1], labels[1:])` -- the per-example causal-LM shift that the documented contract (compute_per_example_loss docstring at _dp_trainer.py:2409-2412 and docs/alignment/trainers.md:114, 'it runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op') tells them to write. Training invokes it per example under vmap; since 25bb4ed7 (#1028) the DEFAULT eval path invokes the same callable once on the batched ModelOutput at _dp_trainer.py:2719-2726, with no rank check. Measured on a 16-example eval set with T=V=4: the true training objective (and the include_for_metrics=['loss'] eval path) is 1.70644, while the default evaluate() reports eval_loss 1.34594 -- a silent ~0.36-nat divergence, because the slice shifted the batch axis and cross_entropy treated the sequence axis as classes. With metric_for_best_model='eval_loss' / load_best_model_at_end / early stopping, the wrong series drives checkpoint selection. When T != V the identical configuration instead raises `RuntimeError: Expected target size [3, 5], got [3, 4]` at eval, so a user whose custom loss previously worked (the batched branch used to ignore compute_loss_func and read output['loss']) now gets a crash. Eval metrics only: no effect on gradients, clipping, noise or the privacy accounting. SFT with loss_type in {'nll','chunked_nll'} reaches the same batched call via _sft_trainer.py:646-656.
